page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-800s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an AMD EPYC processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the instance.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng CPU tests, placing the server in the top 10% of tested instances. Multi-core CPU performance registers in the average tier across stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark suites. Memory performance is strong, with Passmark memory scores placing in the top 25%, though uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths remain in the average tier at 135.4 GB/sec and 68.38 GB/sec respectively. For language model workloads, text generation using a small 135M model is strong, while prompt processing and larger 7B model inference speeds fall within the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-frequency multi-core processing. The primary tradeoff is the moderate 2.0 GHz clock speed and average multi-threaded scaling, which limits its suitability for compute-heavy parallel processing. This configuration is appropriate for in-memory databases, caching layers, software compilation, and moderate-scale web serving or text processing workloads.
